newsitem.title: USA: Clinton intervenes to avert American strike-McCurry.
newsitem.headline: Clinton intervenes to avert American strike-McCurry.

text.p: President Bill Clinton has signed a decision intervening to avert an American Airlines pilots strike, White House spokesman Mike McCurry said on Saturday.

"He's signed it," McCurry said, referring to a decision to name Presidential Emergency Board to study the dispute between American, a unit of Fort Worth-based AMR Corp, and its pilots. The decision effectively postpones any walkout for 60 days.

"Effective February 15, 1997, Presidential Emergency Board No. 233 will convene to investigate and make recommendations for settlement regarding the current dispute between American Airlines and its employees represented by the Allied Pilots Association," the White House said in a brief statement.

The statement named the board's chairman as Robert Harris, a former chairman of the National Mediation Board, a post he held during 1979-1980 and 1982-1983. It named the two other members as Anthony Sinicropi of California and Helen Witt of Pennsylvania, both experienced in mediating labor disputes.
Under the Railway Labor Act, which also covers airlines, the president has the power to declare a national emergency to stop a strike and keep the planes flying.

Shortly after midnight (0500 GMT Saturday) the pilots said they would strike, prompting the president's action within minutes to prevent a grounding of the airline, which carries about 20 percent of the nation's air travelers.
